name: The Richmond Riverside Plane

location.address: Thames towpath beside Richmond Bridge, Richmond TW9

access: Free, public riverside towpath and Terrace Gardens edge in Richmond; open at all times
transport: Richmond station (District line, Overground, National Rail), about 10 minutes walk down to the river by Richmond Bridge
recognise: Stands on the riverside path just upstream of Richmond Bridge, by the landing stages and the Thames visitor centre; it overtops every other tree on the front, a very tall straight London plane with a pale mottled trunk.

photo_candidates.author: Matt Brown
photo_candidates.note: dated 2026-09-20, geotag 51.456511,-0.305169, file named after the tree

verify_notes: On the Great Trees of London list (Trees for Cities, 1987 storm legacy, extended 2008; Wikipedia list gives it as 'over 40 metres in height, one of the tallest London planes in the UK', citing the Great Trees of London Map by Paul Wood). Single naming source for the height, not independently measured, so height_m is 'over 40' from that list only. Alive: Commons photo of the plane dated 2026-09-20 geotagged at the tree. Pin: Wikipedia coordinate 51.456465,-0.304728; photo geotag 51.456511,-0.305169 (camera position, 30 m apart) so approximate. Earlier lead (2026-10-14) was held for no girth; no longer a gate. Species per list: 'London plane'. Age not documented.

name: The Harlington Yew

location.address: St Peter and St Paul churchyard, St Peter's Way, Harlington, Hayes UB3

access: Free, open churchyard; the yew stands opposite the south door of the church
transport: Hayes & Harlington station (Elizabeth line / National Rail), about 1.5 km; buses not checked

location_site.name: St Peter and St Paul churchyard, Harlington

recognise: The ancient yew standing opposite the south door of the church, the one great tree of the churchyard; it was clipped into topiary shapes until about 1825.
verify_notes: Church's own page: 'thought to be at least 1000 years old', stands opposite the south door, may mark the spot where Christianity was first preached; famed 18th to early 19th century for topiary, annual clipping a Whitsun festivity until about 1825. Ancient Yew Group database (record Harlington, site visited 1999, file updated 2025): ancient, girth 587 cm at the ground (their field also reads 494 for the tree id), grid ref TQ08807822, category 'Ancient 5m-7m'. British Museum print record calls it over 900 years old. A 1914 notice said probably more than 1000 years old. 1958 report said half the old yew fell in a gale (per search summary, not verified on a fetched page, so not for the page). The AYG notes the churchyard might be lost to Heathrow expansion plans. Age is the church's claim; age range 900 to 1500 is generous; leave as 'at least 1,000 years' with attribution. Alive: AYG 2025 site file exists; no dated photo checked, so flagged. Pin: church 51.4924,-0.4342 (OSM); churchyard small, tree location only given as 'opposite the south door'.

name: The Chiswick House Cedars

location.address: Chiswick House Gardens, Burlington Lane, Chiswick W4 2RP

official_register.name: Chiswick House and Gardens Trust: Cedars of Lebanon

access: Gardens open daily to visitors (Chiswick House & Gardens Trust gives dawn-til-dusk access; check their site for hours); the ground beneath the Beatles cedar is roped off, the tree cannot be climbed
transport: Chiswick station (South Western Railway) about 10 minutes walk; Turnham Green (District) about 20 minutes
recognise: The great cedars frame the house's garden front; the one filmed by the Beatles in 1966 has a low, huge limb, and stands diagonally across from the statue garden where the 'Paperback Writer' scenes were shot.

photo_candidates.author: Stefan Czap
photo_candidates.note: title Cedar tree, Chiswick House Gardens; geotag 51.48229,-0.26073 is a camera position

photo_candidates.author: Patche99z
photo_candidates.note: two large cedars from the rear of the house

verify_notes: Owner (Chiswick House and Gardens Trust): oldest trees date from the late 1720s when William Kent first worked on the garden; several came directly from Lebanon; avenue of cedars frames the house; prone to drop branches without warning, do not walk under or climb. Planting dates conflict across sources (1720, 1726 from Sutton Court, 1741, 1745), so age is broad. The Beatles' cedar was one of ten trees shortlisted for Woodland Trust Tree of the Year 2025 (BBC 2025-07-11); believed planted in the 1720s per Woodland Trust. Beatles filmed 'Rain' and 'Paperback Writer' promo films there on 20 May 1966 (Bob Whitaker cover photo for the Nowhere Man EP). Result of the 2025 award not established. Pin: no tree-level coordinate found (Friends of Chiswick House tree trail is Cloudflare-blocked from here). Chosen pin is an iNaturalist observation of Cedrus libani (2022-09-19, accuracy 8 m, https://www.inaturalist.org/observations/135647107) in the gardens; other Cedrus libani observations lie 51.4830,-0.2575 and 51.4851,-0.2627, so the cedars are spread across the grounds and the exact Beatles tree is not placed. Approximate. Walk-through garden, so no location_site. Several cedars, folded into one entry as one destination. Alive: iNaturalist Cedrus libani observations in 2025.

name: The Maids of Honour Stone Pine
access: Free, open public green (Richmond Green), open at all times
transport: Richmond station (District line, Overground, National Rail), about 5 minutes walk
recognise: A lone umbrella-shaped stone pine, the only one of its kind among the plane, lime and horse chestnut on the green, on the Maids of Honour Row side near the Old Palace gatehouse.
verify_notes: On the Great Trees of London list (Trees for Cities); Wikipedia's list gives coordinate 51.461379,-0.308673 and notes the tree lost a major limb in August 2026 (cited to an Instagram post; not seen directly, so state only 'lost a limb in 2026' with care or leave out). Alive: two iNaturalist Pinus pinea observations on the green, 2025-10-18 (CC BY) at 51.46160,-0.30848 and 2025-01-25 (CC0) at 51.46167,-0.30824; lifecheck RECENT. Pin from the two observer fixes, about 30 m from the Wikipedia point, so approximate. Age and girth not found in any fetched source; do not invent. Name from the nearby Maids of Honour Row (not verified why the pine carries it).

name: The Syon Park Mulberries
access: Syon Park grounds and gardens are a paid, ticketed entry; the mulberry orchard lies south-east of the house and a separate old mulberry stands in a fenced enclosure in the water meadow towards the river; check syonpark.co.uk for days
transport: Syon Lane station (National Rail), about 15 to 20 minutes walk to the park gate
recognise: Ancient, multi-stemmed mulberries in an orchard south-east of the house; the trunks have layered into rings with the central bole almost gone. One solitary old mulberry stands alone in an enclosure in the water meadow that the house's long gallery looks over, leaning and propped.
verify_notes: Morus Londinium (Tree Register / London mulberry survey) site record for Syon Park, grid TQ 17646 76713 (converted to 51.4772,-0.3074; site-level reference, not a tree), 6 mulberries, tallest 8 m: several ancient multi-stemmed layering mulberries in an orchard SE of the house; a solitary ancient tree in an adjacent field towards the river, probably once part of the orchard. Percy family archives record purchase of 10 mulberries in March 1604 and 6 more in 1645 and 1646; the survey says if all survived up to 10 could be over 416 years old; it also says there is NO evidence for mulberries at Syon in 1548, so the popular claim that William Turner planted it in 1548 (Spitalfields Life blog) is a legend, not a source. 19th-century writers refer to a very old tree with branches touching the ground. Tree Register 2017 visit notes mention the remains and regrowth of an ancient black mulberry possibly the oldest surviving tree on the estate (search summary of the pdf, not read on the page, so treat as a pointer). Age is a derived, broad estimate from the archive purchase dates; 'Heritage Notable' site class. Alive: Morus Londinium record, no dated photo of the individual trunk checked. Tree-level pin not found. Replaces the Kew/Syon mulberry lead of 2026-10-14 for Syon only.
